Isn’t that what’s best for the fans? If the NFL had baseball’s system, Josh Allen would have had a nice run with the Bills and would be playing for the New York Giants. Remember that Paul Skenes Yankees jersey I captured in the parking lot on Opening Day two years ago? It’s unfathomable to think of. View this post on Instagram It’s ironic that the year before baseball shuts down to argue over a cap and floor system that the smallest market in baseball makes it look easy. That shouldn’t rewrite the past or make people forget about While the Rays, Brewers, Guardians, and other small market teams have had successful regular seasons and some postseason success, it’s all about hoisting the trophy in late October. A cap and floor system makes the NFL, NHL, and NBA thrive. In the last 10 years, small markets like the Pittsburgh Penguins, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Florida Panthers have won back-to-back cups. Does market size make any difference in other sports? Nope. So why should it be in pro baseball? When the curtain comes down in 2026, we don’t know when Major League Baseball will play again. But despite what happened in one single postseason, the need for a cap and floor will never change at all.

Rasco via Getty Images This, broadly, is the formula that the Wolves believed would give them the brand of firepower necessary to be able to more effectively stand toe-to-toe with the likes of the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs, who have eliminated them from the last two postseasons. It’s a formula, however, that requires Edwards to remain upright and ambulatory … and, as we learned on Tuesday, that’s something he’s not going to be for a while . Just four games into the season, Edwards needs arthroscopic surgery on his right knee — the same knee in which he experienced recurring issues last season with what’s called patellofemoral pain syndrome, or “runner’s knee.” That ailment cost the All-NBA guard 11 of the Wolves’ final 14 games of the regular season; he needed to have his right knee drained multiple times during Minnesota’s playoff run , too. (He also hyperextended his left knee during the opening round against the Denver Nuggets; he missed just two games, and averaged 23.7 points on 47/38/80 shooting splits after returning.) After spending the bulk of the summer resting up to give that knee time to properly heal , and reportedly feeling fully healthy and operational through Minnesota’s training camp and preseason slate, Edwards reportedly tweaked his knee during the Wolves’ opening-night win over the Miami Heat. You’d be forgiven for not noticing, considering he hung 45 and drilled nine 3-pointers to ruin Giannis Antetokounmpo’s South Beach debut: Despite the tweak, Edwards played on, with observers noticing frequent grimacing , instinctive reaches for that right knee , and the occasional limp. But while he was listed as questionable heading into Monday’s matchup with the Cavaliers, Edwards not only played, but logged 41 minutes, had more total touches ( 82 ) and a higher time of possession ( nine minutes ) than any other player in the game, and finished nearly 40% of Minnesota’s offensive possessions with a shot attempt, foul drawn or turnover — a usage rate that would’ve been a top-five mark for him in each of the last four seasons — all on the second night of a back-to-back. In fairness, he did look awfully good while doing so … … and the Wolves, it seems, didn’t suspect that there was anything more significant going on than the kind of soreness through which superstars of Edwards’ caliber are often expected to play. “It’s a daily situation,” Wolves head coach Chris Finch told reporters before the Cavs game. “I don’t think there’s any long-term concern.” Concerns mounted after the game, though, with subsequent imaging showing “increased issues there,” according to ESPN’s Shams Charania — damage “that was different from what he experienced against the San Antonio Spurs in May,” according to Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic. “It’s not a meniscus,” Wolves president of basketball operations Tim Connelly told reporters at the team’s Wednesday shootaround session. “It’s just a — I don’t want to speak out of school. My liberal arts degree will screw me up. It’s just an arthroscopic clean-up of his knee. … We’ve had a bunch of imaging since the summer, and it changed as of yesterday.” Based on that new information, player and team elected to move forward with a surgical procedure on Thursday, from which Sarah Todd of the Minnesota Star Tribune reports that the Wolves “hope to have [Edwards] back on the court sometime in December.” That might be a tad optimistic. Krawczynski pegs Edwards’ return as more likely to be in January : “As of now, the belief is it’s going to be more than two months .” Two months from Thursday would be Dec. 29. The Wolves’ final game of 2026 comes on New Year’s Eve at home against the Denver Nuggets. If Edwards is back for that, he would have missed 28 games, ensuring that, for the second consecutive year , he’ll be ineligible for year-end awards like Most Valuable Player and the All-NBA teams, and for the supermax salary escalators on his next extension that would come if he were to receive them. The message coming out of Minnatlantasota , though, is that Ant is focused less on putting himself in position to make the top dollar next summer than giving himself the best chance to reach the top of the mountain this spring. “Like we’ve talked about before, there’s only one thing that matters to Ant,” Justin Holland, Edwards’ business manager, said in a statement to The Athletic . “It’s not about individual accolades, All-NBAs or anything like that. It’s a single focus: winning a championship. We’ve seen in a short time what this team is capable of, and know big things are ahead when all are 100%.” That could be especially true in a Western Conference in which the Thunder will likely be without starters Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace for most, if not all, of the regular season , and in which a Spurs team that opened up with losses to Oklahoma City and Houston might have some kinks to iron out as they look to return to the NBA Finals. If the expected powerhouses have more cracks in the armor than might have been anticipated, and if Edwards and the Wolves believe that what they put on tape during those first four games is real, then nothing matters more than entering the postseason as close to full strength as possible — even if that means putting Edwards on ice. “With Anthony, all he wants to do is compete, so he’s doing this kicking and screaming,” Connelly said Wednesday. “But we’re pretty confident that he’ll get out there when he’s right. We don’t know when it’s going to be, but we don’t think it’s going to be something that’s going to cost him the season. … The best thing about what he’s gonna go under is, he’ll be as good as new. It’s not something we’re concerned with long term.” Of course, the rest of the Wolves still have to make it through these next two months without falling too far off the pace in the West. item.description: Source: Michelangelo DeSantis/Shutterstock.com Christian McCaffrey entered another exclusive group during San Francisco’s October 25, 2026, game in Atlanta. McCaffrey already had 36 receiving touchdowns, making the pair the only NFL players with at least 70 rushing and 30 receiving scores. The individual achievement came during San Francisco’s first defeat of the season. A fourth-down run delivers the milestone McCaffrey reached the goal line on San Francisco’s opening possession at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Facing fourth-and-goal from the Atlanta 1, he carried the ball into the end zone to finish the game’s first touchdown drive. The 49ers traveled 64 yards on 10 plays, taking a 7-0 lead with 9:22 remaining in the first quarter. McCaffrey contributed as both a runner and receiver throughout the opening series. That early score also extended his streak to six consecutive games with a rushing touchdown. He matched Raheem Mostert and Derek Loville for the longest such streak by a San Francisco running back since 1970. The result improved the Falcons’ record to 3–4 and ended San Francisco’s unbeaten start to the season. The 49ers committed 4 turnovers, including 2 interceptions by Brock Purdy. Those mistakes proved costly as San Francisco attempted to recover from its early advantage. A thigh problem interrupts his afternoon McCaffrey’s strong start was interrupted by a thigh injury that forced him out for part of the first half. item.title: Does Rays’ Drew Rasmussen expect to pitch in World Series Game 5?
item.description: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Does Rays’ Drew Rasmussen expect to pitch in World Series Game 5? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With the Tampa Bay Rays winning Game 4 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers in 12 innings, 4-3, the team extends the series, which brings questions about who the ball club will trot out to pitch. As the Rays look to keep extending the World Series, one pitcher that could be used again is star Drew Rasmussen , as he speaks on possibly pitching in Game 5 on Wednesday. Speaking after the thrilling win for Tampa Bay, Rasmussen said that he feels “great” and expressed that he would “assume I’m in there” for Game 5, according to Jorge Castillo of ESPN. “I’m probably smoking hot, would be my guess. I mean, we haven’t talked yet. I feel great. So, I’m sure they’re going to kick around some ideas in there for a little bit, but I would assume I’m in there,” Rasmussen said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The last time Rasmussen pitched was in Game 2 of the World Series, where he didn’t have his best outing, throwing 3.2 innings, allowing three earned runs and six hits, while striking out four batters and walking two. “I thought early on my command wasn’t very good,” Rasmussen said after his rough outing, via Sports Illustrated. “I felt like I was falling behind far too often to expect good results. And then from there, they found themselves in some hitters’ counts and were able to find holes.” The Rays believe they can “win four in a row” in the World Series The Rays would finally record one win in the World Series, but it was a grueling victory as after a Cooper Pratt home run for the Brewers in the top of the 12th inning, Tampa Bay would be a hit machine in the bottom of the 12th. After Jonny DeLuca tied the game, Ben Williamson would get the RBI base hit to win the game, as pitcher Nick Martinez believes the Rays “can win four in a row,” via ESPN. It remains to be seen if it can be done as Tampa Bay looks to continue to extend the World Series in Game 5, as fans await to see if Rasmussen pitches. item.title: Career not ending! 44-year-old James Anderson to play in Italy after Lancashire exit
item.description: James Anderson is set to continue his cricket career in Italy after Lancashire decided not to renew his contract. The 44-year-old former England fast bowler will captain and co-own a Naples-based team in a 10-over cricket tournament. Anderson spent 25 years with Lancashire and remains one of England’s most successful bowlers, having played more than 400 matches across formats and taken nearly 1,000 wickets. Anderson takes on new role in Italy The 10-over tournament will run for 12 days at the Roma Cricket Ground from November 18. Anderson will be among the biggest names taking part, alongside players such as Chris Gayle, Shaun Marsh and Dawid Malan, as well as members of Italy’s national team. The competition was created by former professional cricketer Nadeem Shahid and Aamir Akhtar, who helped establish a major cricket tournament in Nepal. Shahid said Italy’s growing interest in cricket and its inclusion in the Olympic Games made the country an attractive destination. "The potential for cricket in Italy made it a big draw," Shahid told Reuters. "One of the things that made it attractive is the Italian Olympic Committee beginning to take it seriously after it became an Olympic sport." Focus on growing cricket beyond the tournament The competition also aims to develop Italian cricket by offering free entry to matches and organising coaching sessions. Anderson’s company, Activate Sport & Leisure, will take part in some of these clinics as Italy works towards developing players for the 2032 Olympic Games in Brisbane. Anderson said his team wants to compete for the title while also supporting the sport’s long-term development in the country. "Of course, we want Napoli Knights to be competitive and challenge for the title, but we also want to contribute to something that continues to grow well beyond the tournament itself," Anderson said.

item.title: What Dan Campbell said about Kerby Joseph’s Lions return
item.description: Junfu Han / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images What Dan Campbell said about Kerby Joseph’s Lions return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions are currently gearing up for their upcoming game on Sunday afternoon against the undefeated divisional rival Minnesota Vikings. The Lions are slated to get a big boost to their defensive backfield at some point in the near future when safety Kerby Joseph returns from a knee issue that has kept him out for the entirety of this season so far. Recently, head coach Dan Campbell spoke on what Joseph brings to the table for Detroit. “Everybody loves Kerby. He’s a good teammate,” he said, per Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network on X, formerly Twitter, via the Lions. The Lions’ defensive backfield as a whole has looked much different than what fans were hoping for this year, as Joseph has been out, in addition to cornerback Brian Branch, who only recently made his season debut after working his way back from a torn Achilles injury. The team is also without Terrion Arnold, who was released by the Lions following his offseason arrest. Overall, the Lions have played mostly solid football this year, and recently proved that they can win without a huge day from the offense in their victory over the divisional rival Green Bay Packers over the weekend. Having Joseph back at some point in the near future should certainly help them out as they look to build toward the playoffs. The Lions and Vikings are slated to kick off on Sunday at 1:00 pm ET. item.title: Hollywood producer Kennedy to head LA28 Olympic ceremony plans
item.description: US producer Kathleen Kennedy has been named to oversee the opening and closing ceremonies at the Los Angeles Olympics and Paralympics in 2028 (Patrick T. Fallon) Oscar-nominated film producer Kathleen Kennedy was named on Wednesday to oversee preparations for the opening and closing ceremonies at the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games in Los Angeles. Kennedy, 73, an eight-time Academy Award nominee whose first film producing credit came on Steven Spielberg's 1982 classic "E.T. The Extra-Terrestrial", will serve as head of ceremonies and content. She will executive produce the opening and closing ceremonies, which will take place at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum and SoFi Stadium. "Kathleen is a legend. She is one of Hollywood's all-time greats, with a rare gift for storytelling," LA28 chairperson and president Casey Wasserman said in a statement. "When the stars align to focus the world's attention on Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympic and Paralympic Games, I can't think of anyone better to conjure the magic of Hollywood than Kathleen." Kennedy, whose other film credits include "Jurassic Park" and "Schindler's List" and the most recent instalments of the "Star Wars" franchise, said she and her husband, fellow producer Frank Marshall, had been longtime Olympic fans. "The Olympics have been a touchstone in my life," Kennedy said. "My husband...and I have attended virtually every Games since Los Angeles in 1984, and sport remains one of the great unifying experiences we share," she said. The Olympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for July 14, 2028, with the Closing Ceremony on July 30. The Paralympic Opening Ceremony is scheduled for August 15, with the Closing Ceremony at the Coliseum on August 27. In a separate announcement on Wednesday, Olympics organisers revealed that the official slogan for the 2028 Games would be "Stars Align" in a nod to Los Angeles's status as the world's entertainment industry capital. "Los Angeles is the place where dreams take flight, and the Olympics show us what's possible when the world unites," Wasserman said in a statement. "We can't wait for the stars to align in 2028 so we can share this moment with everyone." rcw/mw

item.title: Funko releases Bitty Pop! figure of Spurs' Victor Wembanyama
item.description: Even in miniature, Victor Wembanyama still towers over the hardwood. (Funko) Well, at least this itty bitty Wemby looks more like the real thing. Funko, makers of the mega-popular Pop! vinyl figures, has released a new Bitty Pop! mini figure of Spurs star Victor Wembanyama. The nearly-inch-tall likeness comes with his own mini Spurs arena display. The figure and arena retail for $7.99 at the Funko website. A FIGURE OF FUN: The Spurs Coyote scores big on his best day ever in San Antonio Funko's new Bitty Pop! Towns Victor Wembanyama and Basketball Arena features a nearly inch-tall mini figure of the Spurs star with his own Spurs arena display. (Funko) Funko's new Bitty Pop! figure of Spurs star Victor Wembanyama captures the likeness of the 7-foot-4 phenom at a fraction of the scale. (Funko) The Wembanyama Bitty Pop! features the reigning NBA Defensive Player of the Year in his home whites holding a basketball in his right hand with his customary arm sleeve above the wrist. The display arena sports the Spurs logo on just about every surface, including the hardwood and scoreboard. And yes, there's a basketball hoop for added, ahem, realism. The Bitty Pop! figure comes in a hard acrylic display case with a detachable bottom lid, per the product description. The lid doubles as a base for the figure, so you can display that thumb-sized titan in the accompanying arena or anywhere else. Just keep the little choking hazard away from kids and pets and the Halloween candy. How does a Bitty Pop! figure measure up to standard Pop! figures? Funko's size chart shows just how tiny it is. (Funko) Bitty, indeed. (Funko) Wembanyama's new mini Mini-Me is just the latest in a line of Pop! figures depicting the towering talent at small scale. There is, of course, the standard Pop! figure, which dropped in 2024. Funko also released a Wembanyama Pop! in his Fiesta-swatch City Edition Uniform, another in his white Association Edition Jersey and another in his silver Statement Edition Jersey. From left, Standard Funko Pop! figure of Spurs star Victor Wembanyama and City Edition Uniform figure. (Funko) From left, Association Edition Jersey Funko Pop! figure of Spurs star Victor Wembanyama and Statement Edition Jersey figure. (Funko) The standard Pop! retails for $14.99, while the Association and Statement jersey figures are on sale at the Funko website for $10.49. No surprise, the colorful City Edition figure is sold out. The Bitty Wemby follows the release of Wembanyama's first official action figure by McFarlane Toys. That 6-inch figure features a not-quite-right likeness of the French phenom in his road blacks with a display base and basketball. Maybe next time try dots for eyes? item.title: How help is coming for Penn State football and Linebacker U vs Purdue
item.description: The thinnest Penn State football position is finally getting some much needed help. What will it mean for Saturday's suddenly-critical showdown in Beaver Stadium against unranked Purdue? The Nittany Lions are moving Iowa State transfer Marcus Neal, Jr. from safety to linebacker, head coach Matt Campbell confirmed on Wednesday . He also added that backup linebacker, Cam Smith, will finally return to action after missing the previous five games to injury. The hope is that it boosts a linebacker group working with only main players − starters Tony Rojas and Kooper Ebel and backup Cael Brezina. Neal transferred to Penn State, along with Ebel, Brezina and more than 20 others, with a standout resume. He recorded 11 tackles for loss last season, made two interceptions and was named the Big 12 Defensive Player of the Week against Kansas State. But Neal has seemed to struggle to fit into his safety role with the Nittany Lions. He showed inconsistent tackling throughout, though he has forced two fumbles and recovered another. He started five games but was benched for the White Out against USC. Neal's size (6-foot-1, 216 pounds) should help at linebacker. “I just think for Marcus, it allows his talent and his ability to be at a place where we can use it even more, not only in first and second down, but multiplicity and situational football, too,“ Campbell said. "It’s about trying to find ways to get our best players on the field and put those guys in position to be the best within the scheme. "Marcus just wants to play. There’s only one speed with Marcus. (We're) really excited about finding the right fit for him and the right home for him." Meanwhile, Smith, a redshirt freshman, should see his first backup work since the mid-September game at Temple. He had hoped to cleared to play two weeks ago at Michigan, following an unspecified injury recovery, but was held out for precautionary reasons, Campbell said. Campbell called Smith one of the team's "MVPs" during its off-week. These moves could help relieve some pressure on the other linebackers, particularly Rojas, who has turned in an All-American effort through this first seven games. He leads the Lions in tackles (56), tackles for loss (10.5) and interceptions (two). He also, impressively enough, has more sacks (five) than the rest of the defense combined (four). item.title: Big Ten adopts new conference rules to raising financial cap, aligning with Protect College Sports Act
item.description: The Big Ten Conference released a statement regarding their preparation for framework regarding the Protect College Sports Act on Wednesday. Presidents and Chancellors from the conference met Tuesday ahead of this announcement. Yahoo Sports’ Ross Dellenger provided more context to the announcement. It involved a financial cap, as well as the creation of new rules, strict ones at that, regarding third party NIL. $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage “The Big Ten has adopted these new conference rules that align with the athlete compensation framework in the Protect College Sports Act, raising the cap from $21.6M to $49M, creating strict rules on school-affiliated 3rd-party NIL and establishing penalties for exceeding the cap,” Dellenger wrote. “Approved by the conference’s chancellors and presidents on Oct. 28, the Big Ten is adopting a conference-level rule limiting member institution involvement in third-party NIL agreements in preparation for the anticipated passage of the Protect College Sports Act (PCSA),” a Big Ten release also read. “The conference’s chancellors and presidents continue to remain in unanimous support of the PCSA and look to demonstrate their commitment to it with the new rule.” Big Ten preparing for Protect College Sports Act A statement from the Big Ten Council of Chancellors/Presidents Chair Pamela Whitten on behalf of the Big Ten’s presidents and chancellors was also released Wednesday. “While we await the passage of the Protect College Sports Act, which has our full support, it is imperative our member institutions can begin to plan, budget and build their rosters approximating the act’s economic structure,” it said. “Our institutions remain in full support of the Protect College Sports Act and this rule not only allows for a much smoother transition into the policies put in place by the act once it passes, but demonstrates our commitment to it.” “The timing of the Big Ten rule is intended to both guide member institutions and alert the public as to Big Ten institutional constraints in upcoming NIL discussions with student-athletes,” the Big Ten’s statement continued in part. “The rule effectively requires Big Ten institutions to initiate the financial and operational mechanisms necessary to comply with PCSA limits in advance of upcoming signing and transfer portal windows. The rule is effective immediately and each institution and its lead athletics staff must attest their compliance with the rule. “This policy applies to institutional action only as student-athletes remain free to pursue NIL opportunities with any entity (associated or non-associated) on their own. The Big Ten rule does not replace any existing rules or policies. Big Ten institutions remain subject to all current NCAA rules and College Sports Commission (CSC) policies, including those regarding valid business purpose, permissible range of compensation and submission and review of third-party NIL agreements.”

item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo named BOAT winner! France Football readers vote Portuguese icon's 2008 triumph ahead of Lionel Messi's 2012 campaign
item.description: TOPSHOT-FBL-EUR-C1-MANUTD-AALBORG - AFP Cristiano Ronaldo has officially been crowned the winner of the inaugural B.O.A.T. (Ballon d'Or of All Time) award following a global fan vote. The legendary Portuguese forward saw his iconic 2008 campaign at Manchester United recognized as the greatest individual year in the history of the prestigious trophy. Ronaldo edges Messi in historic vote In a move that has reignited the eternal debate over footballing supremacy, France Football introduced a unique accolade following their most recent gala. The B.O.A.T. award was designed to settle which specific Ballon d'Or winning season stands above all others in the annals of the sport. Ronaldo emerged victorious, with his sensational 2008 form for Manchester United securing the top spot in the public poll. The result sees the Al-Nassr star narrowly beat out his career-long rival Lionel Messi. Specifically, the voters preferred Ronaldo's first Golden Ball triumph over Messi's record-breaking 2012 season, a year in which the Argentine famously netted 91 goals for club and country. New criteria for the B.O.A.T. award Unlike the traditional Ballon d'Or, which relies on a panel of international journalists to determine the winner, the B.O.A.T. award shifted the power directly to the supporters. France Football opened the voting to its digital audience, allowing fans to weigh in on which version of their favorite legends truly deserved the ultimate crown of the greatest of all time. The nomination list featured only those who had secured multiple Golden Balls during their playing days. This prestigious group included the likes of Johan Cruyff, Michel Platini, Marco van Basten, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Kevin Keegan and Franz Beckenbauer, alongside Real Madrid icon Alfredo Di Stefano and Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazario. Fans pay to crown their idols Participating in this historic poll came with a unique catch, as users were required to pay a one-euro fee to cast their vote. To encourage participation despite the fee, the organizers entered all voters into a prize draw for two tickets to the 2027 Ballon d'Or ceremony. The initiative proved popular, with thousands of fans opting to pay for the privilege of backing their chosen era of greatness. The data revealed that over 5,000 individuals actually voted multiple times to ensure their favorite player came out on top. Ronaldo and Messi dominate top 12 Ronaldo and Messi completely dominated the voting, occupying the top 12 spots between them. It was not until 13th place that another player broke their stranglehold, with Brazilian legend Ronaldo Nazario claiming the position thanks to his memorable 2002 Ballon d'Or triumph.

item.title: Joe Brady announces DJ Moore, Ed Oliver will return to Bills practice
item.description: We’ve hardly seen DJ Moore and Ed Oliver this season for the Buffalo Bills, as the two veterans have played 33.9% and 26.7% of their unit’s snaps respectively to date this season. But after multi-game absences for each, they’ll both be back on the practice field today in preparation for Sunday’s contest against the Ravens in Week 8: #Bills HC Joe Brady says Ed Oliver will be out there on the practice field today. He says they built their vision of the defense around Oliver. — Andy Young (@AndyYoungTV) October 28, 2026 Brady made promises about Oliver’s return in Week 8 just yet and had a similar stance on Moore, who missed the last 2.5 games after aggravating his AC joint sprain in Week 4 against the Patriots. #Bills HC Joe Brady on DJ Moore potentially returning to action this week: "It was tough for him not to play in those games…it'll be nice to see him back on the football field today" and they'll see where things go this week. — Andy Young (@AndyYoungTV) October 28, 2026 Of course, if one or both of these established stars can return for the field — huge boost for the Bills on both sides of the ball. The practice designations for Moore and Oliver will be critical to monitor throughout the rest of the week as Buffalo gets ready to return from the bye at home against the Ravens this weekend.

item.title: ‘An extreme rarity for an NFL owner’: Falcons owner Arthur Blank donates to AOC
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL owners have long been some of the most reliable donors in Republican politics, and the 2026 midterms have been no exception. But one owner has taken a very different approach this election cycle. According to a new report, Atlanta Falcons owner Arthur Blank donated to the reelection campaign of Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, a self-described democratic socialist who is widely seen as a potential 2028 presidential contender. Blank has also spent hundreds of thousands of dollars trying to help Democrats win back the Senate. NFL Owners Lean Right NFL owners have spent more than $18 million on candidates and committees in the midterms, and “nearly all of it has gone to Republicans,” according to Front Office Sports , which reviewed Federal Election Commission records. That includes huge donations from some of the league’s most prominent owners. Broncos co-owner Rob Walton has spent nearly $9 million backing Republican candidates and committees, while Cowboys owner Jerry Jones gave $1 million to Donald Trump’s MAGA Inc. Only two owners have given heavily to Democrats this cycle, and Blank is one of them. Blank Backs AOC Blank, the Home Depot co-founder who bought the Falcons in 2002, gave $3,500 to Ocasio-Cortez, who is running for her fifth term in the House. Front Office Sports called the donation “an extreme rarity for an NFL owner.” A spokesperson for Blank confirmed his donations but declined to comment further. item.title: Wrexham fined for fielding ineligible players
item.description: Callum O'Hare (left) and Issa Kabore (right) joined Wrexham on permanent deals during the 2026 summer transfer window [Getty Images/Shutterstock] Wrexham have been fined £75,000 - of which £25,000 is suspended - by the English Football League after two incidents of fielding ineligible players this season. The EFL ruled that Issa Kabore and Callum O'Hare were ineligible to feature in Wrexham's games against Birmingham and Millwall, respectively. Kabore came off the bench in Wrexham's 2-1 defeat by Birmingham City on 28 August, despite his Home Office 'right to work' documents not being correctly uploaded. O'Hare, having joined from Sheffield United the day before, was an unused substitute in Wrexham's 3-0 win at Millwall on 2 September, though his documentation was not uploaded in time. A club statement read: "We can confirm that Wrexham AFC has reached an agreed decision with the EFL concerning two breaches relating to player eligibility." Unlucky seven? Wrexham aim to buck bizarre trend Burkina Faso international Kabore spent last season on loan with Wrexham but made his move from Manchester City permanent in the summer. He returned to the Racecourse Ground on the eve of the contest with Birmingham, signing a three-year deal with the north Wales side. The 25-year-old has featured 10 times in the Championship so far this season. O'Hare also put pen to paper on a three-year contract with Wrexham in the summer after opting to leave Sheffield United. Wrexham - currently 17th in the second tier after 12 games - are understood to be actively improving measures at the club to avoid future issues. They are thought to be hiring a club secretary in addition to improving administrative training. A club official told BBC Sport Wales that the incidents involving Kabore and O'Hare were not the fault of boss Phil Parkinson, the club's coaching staff or new sporting director Steve Nickson - who was not officially appointed to his role until 7 September. The Wrexham statement added: "The club is taking the appropriate steps to prevent such issues occurring in the future." Latest Wrexham news, analysis and fan views Wrexham AFC

item.title: Indian Premier League cricket surges with value and parity
item.description: (Photo by AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images With an estimated 2.5 billion fans worldwide, cricket ranks No. 2 among the world’s most popular sports, trailing only soccer. A huge part of that is fandom in India, and within that the Indian Premier League (IPL) has been a driving force in turning T20 cricket from a fast-paced offshoot of the game, to the most beloved format in the sport. Boasting eight different champions since the league was formed 18 years ago, the 10-team IPL has been thriving because of its parity, unique drafting system, and competition, which draws the best players in the world to India for the IPL season. The only missing part of the equation has been the finances behind the scenes, and now we have details. Our colleagues over at Sportico have published the first-ever team valuations for the IPL , and it shows the overall health of the league. Leading the charge are the Mumbai Indians, representing the largest city in the country. They are the only team to clear the $2B mark, which isn’t surprising — but what does turn heads is how close the competition is behind them when it comes to team worth. This is a league that is not just surviving, but thriving, and is becoming the litmus test every cricketing nation is trying to follow. The wait is on until the IPL returns in March of 2027, but it’s worth diving back into what made the 2026 season tick in terms of just how close the competition was. A back-to-back champion, but LOTS of competition Royal Challengers Bengaluru went back-to-back thanks to the eternally peerless batting of Virat Kohli and Devdutt Padikkal, but don’t let that muddy the water into thinking that Bengaluru is a team running their opponents off the wicket. They finished the season with a 9-5 overall record, but so did the Gujarat Titans and Sunrisers Hyderabad — while the Rajasthan Royals and Punjab Kings were narrowly behind at 8-6 and 7-6-1, respectively. That means that half the league was separated by a single win or less, making the four-team playoff system in the IPL a total toss-up. Moreover, every team in the league finished with at least four wins in their 14 games — meaning that nobody is truly bottomed out. Still home to the most fascinating draft in sports The IPL “draft” is more open free agency than it is a draft in the strictest terms we know from sports in the United States. Players who are set to hit the market enter the IPL Draft Auction, which is held each year, allowing teams to put their money where they mouths are to bid for a player’s services in an open venue, with the high-bidder getting the chance to transform their team. item.title: ‘Legendary run’: NBA world reacts to Ernie Johnson career announcement
item.description: The 2026-27 NBA season will officially mark the end of an era for legendary broadcaster Ernie Johnson, Johnson, 70, announced Wednesday that this will be his final season hosting Inside the NBA . Johnson has led the popular studio show since 1990, first for more than three decades on TNT and TBS and this season on ESPN. Along the way, he has cultivated a reputation as one of the best in the business both on and off set. “Just to be clear, I’m not retiring,” said Johnson , who has worked in media since 1979. “Just cutting back. I’ll still do March Madness and other projects for TNT and CBS, and I’ve just started a new production company called 32 Bowties geared toward telling feel-good stories in sports. So this is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page.” It’s time. https://t.co/h1qNwsnkUY — Ernie Johnson (@TurnerSportsEJ) October 28, 2026 Lots of love for a legend Johnson is beloved by fans and fellow media members alike, so it’s no surprise that today’s news has been met with an outpouring of love on social media. “ A legendary run for Ernie Johnson on Inside the NBA. Going to cherish this final season with him in the host chair. An all-time great,” wrote ESPN’s Field Yates. “A treasure. World class human and one of the very best to ever do it,” added Scott Van Pelt . “The greatest studio host, bar none, of any sports show. Godspeed to the Goat, who is a better person than he is a host. It was an honor to work with you, EJ,” wrote The Athletic’s David Aldridge , Johnson’s former Turner Sports colleague. “The king is leaving . . . Long live the king,” one NBA fan chimed in . “Ernie is one of the GOATs. Completely relatable, people person,” said BYUtv Sports Nation’s Jarom Jordan. “One time in the mid 2010s he visited BYU to do a story on Dave Rose’s cancer recovery. He came over to BYUtv and I gave him a tour. He was gracious and kind. The same guy you see on screen.” “Thank you for the memories,” another fan said simply . Enjoy Ernie while you can Obviously, Johnson isn’t completely going away, as he made clear in his announcement. Still, Inside the NBA is what he is best known for, and the program just won’t be the same if it goes on without him. Thankfully, we still have the rest of this season to soak up as much of E.J. as we can. item.title: Burnley appoint ex-Basel boss Celestini as head coach
item.description: Before moving into coaching, Fabio Celestini played for clubs including Lausanne, Marseille, Levante and Getafe [Burnley FC] Burnley have appointed Fabio Celestini as their new head coach, four days after the sacking of Nicky Hayen. The 50-year-old led FC Basel to a domestic double in 2024-25, winning the Swiss Super League title and the Swiss Cup. But having mainly managed in Switzerland, Celestini was most recently in charge of CSKA Moscow, with whom he won the Russian Super Cup. "I look at Burnley and I see a club with big potential and players with real quality, who can help us achieve our supporters' ambitions," he said. "I know the situation we are in, and I have lived it before. Our supporters deserve to see a team playing with belief from the first whistle." Burnley appoint Lopez to lead Clarets search for new manager Hayen sacked by Burnley after just 14 games Burnley owners seek to lift strike-off notice Celestini arrives to take charge of a Clarets side who have started life back in the Championship badly, having won just once in the league this season to leave them in 22nd position in the table. Their poor form stretches back to a torrid Premier League campaign last term, and the club are without a win at home in the league for over a year. Earlier this week, Diego Lopez was appointed as director of football and given the task of finding a new manager after Hayen left in the aftermath of Saturday's 4-1 defeat by Lincoln City. "Fabio brings the passion, experience and knowledge we were looking for," Lopez said. "He showed extraordinary determination and conviction to come to Burnley. "We want people who truly want to be here and help this club grow. Fabio is a clear example of that." Details of Celestini's contract have not been disclosed by the club. A former midfielder who won 35 caps for Switzerland, he began his managerial career with Italian club Terracina. As well as Basel and CSKA Moscow, he has also had spells at Lausanne - his principal club as a player, Lucerne, Lugano and Sion. He left CSKA by mutual agreement in May after 11 months with the Russian Premier League side. Latest Burnley news, analysis and fan views Ask about Burnley - what do you want to know?

The New York Jets recently reached a new low on the 2026 NFL season with a tough home loss to the Miami Dolphins, giving Miami its first win of the year in the process. The Jets now sit at 2-5 on the season, with calls for the team to fire head coach Aaron Glenn growing louder by the day. However, it still might be a while before such a scenario could take place, per the latest reports. “Most people I talk to think Aaron Glenn will get to coach through the end of this season before the team evaluates the two-year sample and decides whether to bring him back for a third,” reported NFL insider Dan Graziano of ESPN. That said, Glenn still has some major areas of concern as a head coach, including most notably his clock management, which has been a disaster on multiple occasions during his tenure at the helm in New York. Still, it seems that Glenn will be afforded every opportunity possible to work through the struggles and try to get the Jets into something resembling a competitive football team. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. item.content:encoded: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn.
